failure_modes: Survivorship bias. The universe is screened from today's index membership, so twelve years of survivorship run in the candidate's favour. Direction is named in advance: it inflates momentum more than buy-and-hold, so a PASS here would be suspect while a FAIL is if anything understated.
Benign period. 2014-2019 contains no COVID crash and no 2022 bear market, which flatters any long-only trend rule.
Low trade count. A concentrated top-decile rule places few trades, so the per-trade confidence interval will be wide and an INCONCLUSIVE significance result must not be read as support.
A PASS would still not be permission to enable anything. It would be one period, one parameterisation, and would need the full walk-forward and the live gate before it meant anything.
spec.prior: EDGE claims stand at 0 for 7 entering this test. The honest prior is that this fails too: a rule published thirty-three years ago and widely known has had a third of a century to be arbitraged away. What makes the result worth having is not the probability of passing but that no selection step exists, so the verdict cannot be an artifact of choosing.
spec.title: Pre-specified cross-sectional momentum (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993), no selection

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP, and it is severe here — worse than in any previous section. The universe is screened from TODAY'S S&P 1500 membership, so every company that went bankrupt or was delisted in the 2008 crisis is absent by construction. The crash is therefore systematically softened, and long-only momentum benefits most from that. Direction named in advance: this inflates every arm, so a PASS here would be weak evidence while a FAIL is strong.

The screen measures liquidity on the FIRST calendar year only (2007), so universe selection cannot peek at the test window. That is a guard, not a guarantee: 2007 liquidity itself reflects pre-crisis conditions.

Three arms share a snapshot and a universe, so their results are strongly correlated. "All three moved" is therefore much weaker evidence than three independent confirmations, and must not be read as such.
Low trade count. A top-decile rule places few trades, so per-arm confidence intervals will be wide and an INCONCLUSIVE significance result is not support.

A PASS is not permission to enable anything. It would be one family, one period, one universe construction — and it would still owe a walk-forward on a period with no survivorship advantage before it meant anything.
spec.prior: This fails. EDGE claims stand at 0 for 8, and §35 already ran xsmom-12-1 on 2014-2019 where it lost 4.04% while the market gained 90.41%. The reason to run it anyway is that 2007-2013 is the first period this repository has ever scored that contains a real bear market, and §35's registration named "benign period" as a failure mode that has stood unanswered since. A three-arm family requirement also makes a lucky single-arm result impossible to mistake for an effect. If momentum has any regime in which it earns its keep, a crisis is the most-claimed one; if it fails here too, that claim is answered on this repository's own data rather than by assertion.
spec.title: Cross-sectional momentum family coherence, 2007-2013 (incl. the GFC)
